title: Drinking water maximum contaminant levels practice questions
description: Free practice questions on federal drinking water MCLs and MRDLs in 40 CFR 141 Subpart G. Every answer quotes and links the rule.

questions.topic: Effective dates and who the limits cover
questions.question: What effective date does 141.60(a)(4) set for the PFAS entries in 141.61(c)(2)(i) through (vii)?

options.A: January 17, 1994

questions.explanation: 141.60(a)(4): "The effective date for § 141.61(c)(2)(i) through (vii) is April 26, 2029."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.60, Effective dates (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Effective dates and who the limits cover
questions.question: Under 141.62(b), which systems does the fluoride MCL in paragraph (b)(1) apply to?

options.A: Community and non-transient, non-community water systems
options.B: Community, non-transient non-community and transient non-community water systems

questions.explanation: 141.62(b) states that the MCL "specified in paragraph (b)(1) of this section only applies to community water systems."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.62, Maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which technologies does 141.61(b) identify as the best technology for the organic MCLs in 141.61(a) and (c) other than PFAS?

options.A: Granular activated carbon, packed tower aeration or oxidation, as shown in table 2
options.B: Anion exchange, reverse osmosis and nanofiltration

questions.explanation: 141.61(b) identifies "granular activated carbon (GAC), packed tower aeration (PTA), or oxidation (OX)" for the organic contaminants in (a) and (c), "except for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.61, Maximum contaminant levels for organic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does the 141.61(c)(2) table (effective April 26, 2029 under 141.60(a)(4)) state the MCL for the Hazard Index PFAS (HFPO-DA, PFBS, PFHxS and PFNA)?
questions.explanation: The MCL row for "Hazard Index PFAS (HFPO-DA, PFBS, PFHxS, and PFNA)" reads "1 (unitless)"; the Hazard Index is "the sum of component hazard quotients (HQs)".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.61, Maximum contaminant levels for organic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does the MCL column of the 141.61(c)(2) PFAS table (effective April 26, 2029 under 141.60(a)(4)) show for PFBS?

options.A: No individual MCL

questions.explanation: The PFBS row reads "No individual MCL"; its entry in the column headed "HBWC (mg/l) for Hazard Index calculation" is 0.002.

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.61, Maximum contaminant levels for organic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Hazard Index footnote in 141.61(c)(2), how is each component hazard quotient calculated?

options.A: By multiplying the PFAS concentration by 4.0
options.B: By averaging the four PFAS results over a calendar year
options.C: By dividing the measured PFAS concentration in water by its health-based water concentration in the same units
options.D: By subtracting the PFOA result from the PFOS result

questions.explanation: Hazard quotients "are calculated by dividing the measured component PFAS concentration in water by the relevant health-based water concentration when expressed in the same units".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.61, Maximum contaminant levels for organic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these 141.62(b) MCLs applies to transient non-community water systems as well as to community and non-transient, non-community water systems?

options.A: Arsenic

questions.explanation: The MCLs "specified in (b)(7), (b)(8), and (b)(9) of this section apply to community water systems; non-transient, non-community water systems; and transient non-community water systems." Nitrite is "(8) Nitrite"; barium and arsenic apply to community and non-transient, non-community systems, and fluoride "only applies to community water systems."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.62, Maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which systems and which MCL does the small system compliance technology table in 141.62(d) address?

options.A: Systems serving more than 10,000 persons, for all inorganic MCLs
options.B: Systems with fewer than 500 service connections, for the fluoride MCL
options.C: Transient non-community water systems, for the nitrate MCL
options.D: Systems serving 10,000 persons or fewer, for the arsenic MCL

questions.explanation: 141.62(d) identifies "the affordable technology, treatment technique, or other means available to systems serving 10,000 persons or fewer for achieving compliance with the maximum contaminant level for arsenic".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.62, Maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: 141.62(c) identifies best available technologies for the inorganic contaminants in 141.62(b) with one exception. Which contaminant is left out?

options.A: Arsenic

questions.explanation: 141.62(c) covers the MCLs "for inorganic contaminants identified in paragraph (b) of this section, except fluoride".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.62, Maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to the key to the BAT table in 141.62(c), for which systems is coagulation/filtration not a BAT?

options.A: Systems with fewer than 500 service connections

questions.explanation: The key reads "2 = Coagulation/Filtration (not BAT for systems <500 service connections)".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.62, Maximum contaminant levels for inorganic contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Beginning April 1, 2016, which of these events is one of the conditions in 141.63(c) that puts a system out of compliance with the E. coli MCL?

options.A: A single routine sample is total coliform-positive and all repeat samples are negative
options.B: The system collects more routine samples than required
options.C: The system fails to test for E. coli when any repeat sample tests positive for total coliform
options.D: A routine sample is collected on a holiday

questions.explanation: Condition (c)(4) is: "The system fails to test for E. coli when any repeat sample tests positive for total coliform."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Beginning April 1, 2016, for what period must a public water system determine compliance with the E. coli MCL under 141.63(d)?

options.A: As a running annual average of quarterly results
options.B: For each month in which it is required to monitor for total coliforms
options.D: As a locational running annual average at each sample site

questions.explanation: A system "must determine compliance with the MCL for E. coli in paragraph (c) of this section for each month in which it is required to monitor for total coliforms."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For the public notification requirements in subpart Q, how does 141.63(c) describe a violation of the E. coli MCL?

options.A: It may pose an acute risk to health
options.B: It is a monitoring and reporting violation only
options.D: It is treated as a secondary standard exceedance

questions.explanation: "For purposes of the public notification requirements in subpart Q of this part, violation of the MCL may pose an acute risk to health."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.63, Maximum contaminant levels (MCLs) for microbiological contaminants (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For the subpart V TTHM and HAA5 MCLs in 141.64(b)(2), what best available technology does 141.64(b)(2)(iii) list for consecutive systems serving fewer than 10,000, for the disinfected water they buy or otherwise receive?

options.A: Control of ozone treatment process
options.D: Improved distribution system and storage tank management to reduce residence time

questions.explanation: The (b)(2)(iii) table, which "applies only to the disinfected water that consecutive systems buy or otherwise receive", lists "Systems serving <10,000: Improved distribution system and storage tank management to reduce residence time".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.64, Maximum contaminant levels for disinfection byproducts (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 141.64(a)(2) identify as the best available technology for bromate?

options.A: Enhanced coagulation plus GAC10
options.B: Control of ozone treatment process to reduce production of bromate
options.C: Use of chloramines for disinfectant residual maintenance

questions.explanation: The BAT table lists for bromate: "Control of ozone treatment process to reduce production of bromate".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.64, Maximum contaminant levels for disinfection byproducts (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For community and non-transient, non-community water systems, what compliance date does 141.64(a)(1) set for the bromate and chlorite MCLs for a subpart H system serving fewer than 10,000 persons?

options.A: January 1, 2002

questions.explanation: "Subpart H systems serving fewer than 10,000 persons and systems using only ground water not under the direct influence of surface water must comply with this paragraph (a) beginning January 1, 2004."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.64, Maximum contaminant levels for disinfection byproducts (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does 141.65(c) identify as the best technology, treatment techniques, or other means available for achieving compliance with the MRDLs?

options.A: Control of treatment processes to reduce disinfectant demand and control of disinfection treatment processes to reduce disinfectant levels
options.B: Enhanced coagulation or enhanced softening, plus GAC10
options.C: Control of ozone treatment process to reduce production of bromate

questions.explanation: 141.65(c) identifies "control of treatment processes to reduce disinfectant demand and control of disinfection treatment processes to reduce disinfectant levels."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.65, Maximum residual disinfectant levels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.65(b)(2), which transient non-community water systems must comply with the chlorine dioxide MRDL?

options.A: All transient non-community systems, whatever disinfectant they use
options.C: Only those serving 10,000 or more persons that use chlorine
options.D: Those using chlorine dioxide as a disinfectant or oxidant

questions.explanation: Each compliance date in 141.65(b)(2) covers systems "using chlorine dioxide as a disinfectant or oxidant", which "must comply with the chlorine dioxide MRDL".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.65, Maximum residual disinfectant levels (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 141.66(b), how is the combined radium-226 and radium-228 value determined?

options.A: By taking the higher of the two results
options.C: By adding the results of the radium-226 analysis and the radium-228 analysis
options.D: By using the radium-226 result alone

questions.explanation: "The combined radium-226 and radium-228 value is determined by the addition of the results of the analysis for radium-226 and the analysis for radium-228."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What does the gross alpha particle activity MCL in 141.66(c) exclude?

options.A: Radium-226

questions.explanation: The MCL covers "gross alpha particle activity (including radium-226 but excluding radon and uranium)".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 141.66, Maximum contaminant levels for radionuclides (as of Nov 3, 2026)
